title: Mexicana de Aviación 940

location.name: El Carbón mountain, Sierra Madre Occidental

summary: Boeing 727 crashed into a mountain in the Sierra Madre Occidental northwest of Mexico City during climb. The crash was caused by an explosion originating in the wheel well from an overheated wheel that had suffered high drag from faulty brakes during takeoff. Fire from the explosion ignited fuel and hydraulic liquids, which grew rapidly and caused severe structural damage. The aircraft suffered structural failure from the fire and crashed into the mountainside, killing all 159 passengers and 8 crew members. The investigation found faulty brakes caused the wheel to overheat during the takeoff roll, initiating the catastrophic sequence.
probable_cause: Faulty brakes caused high drag during the takeoff run, which resulted in wheel overheat. The overheated wheel then exploded in the wheel well, igniting fuel and hydraulic liquids. The resulting fire grew rapidly and caused extensive structural damage including fuselage melting, leading to in-flight structural failure and crash.

factors.evidence: Faulty brakes were noted as contributing to wheel drag and overheat during takeoff.
Wheel explosion in wheel well released high-energy event that ignited fuel and hydraulic systems.
Fire ensued as explosion ignited fuel and hydraulic liquids, causing fire to quickly grow.
Aircraft suffered structural failure due to severity of fire causing large area of fuselage to melt.
Aircraft crashed into mountainside following structural failure.

events.text: Aircraft begins takeoff roll from runway 05 left with 159 passengers and 8 crew, aircraft felt heavier than usual and accelerated less than expected.
Captain orders first officer to increase thrust to 100 percent, aircraft takes off approximately 11 seconds later than estimated.
At 29,400 feet altitude during climb, explosion rocks fuselage, breaking cabin floor and causing loss of cabin pressure.
Flight attendant reports fire inside cabin originating from floor below, smoke entering cabin and rear fuselage becoming hot.
Fire grows larger, intense heat causes smoke visible trailing from tailplane, aircraft becomes harder to control and starts losing altitude.
Crew contacts ATC requesting emergency landing in Mexico City, but aircraft continues losing control due to fire intensity.
Aircraft crashes into El Carbón mountain in Sierra Madre Occidental northwest of Mexico City as structural failure progresses.

title: Aeroflot 2306
summary: Aeroflot Flight 2306, a Tupolev Tu-134AK, crashed on July 2, 1986 during an emergency landing after departing Syktyvkar on a domestic flight from Vorkuta to Moscow. The aircraft had sustained 7,989 pressurization cycles and 13,988 flight hours prior to the accident.

factors.evidence: crashed on 2 July 1986 during an emergency landing

events.text: Tupolev Tu-134AK crashed during emergency landing after departing Syktyvkar

notes: Text provides only basic aircraft information and no details on accident causes

title: 1986 Sudan Airways Fokker F-27 shootdown
summary: On 16 August 1986 a Sudan Airways Fokker F-27 Friendship 400M was performing a scheduled domestic passenger flight from Malakal to Khartoum when it was shot down by SPLA (Sudan People's Liberation Army) militants shortly after takeoff. The aircraft was struck by a Soviet-made Strela 2 surface-to-air missile fired by a Shilluk contingent of the SPLA using a missile reportedly captured from the Sudanese army. All 60 people aboard the aircraft were killed. This incident occurred in the context of the Second Sudanese Civil War, when SPLA militants had announced they would shoot down all unauthorized military or civilian aircraft.
probable_cause: The aircraft was struck by a Soviet-made Strela 2 surface-to-air missile fired by SPLA militants during an armed conflict.

factors.evidence: SPLA militants announced they would shoot down all unauthorized military or civilian aircraft, and shot down the aircraft with a Soviet-made Strela 2 surface-to-air missile
the aircraft was brought down by the missile shortly after takeoff

events.text: The Fokker F-27 took off from Malakal Airport
Shortly after takeoff from Malakal the aircraft was brought down by a Soviet-made Strela 2 surface-to-air missile fired by a Shilluk contingent of the SPLA
All 60 people on board the aircraft were killed

title: Aeroméxico 498
summary: Aeroméxico Flight 498 collided with a Piper PA-28 Cherokee that entered the Los Angeles Terminal Control Area without clearance. The Piper was not equipped with a Mode C transponder and was not visible to either the DC-9 crew or ATC radar. The collision sheared the top of the Piper's cockpit and severely damaged the DC-9's tail surfaces. The DC-9 crashed into a residential neighborhood in Cerritos, killing 64 on the aircraft, 3 in the Piper, and 15 on the ground.
probable_cause: The Piper entered the TCA without required clearance and did not have the transponder or warning systems that would have alerted the DC-9 or ATC to its presence. Neither pilot saw the other aircraft. ATC was distracted by another unauthorized aircraft in the area.

factors.evidence: LAX was not equipped with automatic warning systems
The ATC had been distracted by another unauthorized private flight, a Grumman AA-5B Tiger, entering the TCA
Neither pilot appeared to have attempted any evasive maneuvers, because neither pilot sighted the other aircraft
The Piper collided with the DC-9, shearing off the top of the Piper's cockpit and severely damaging the DC-9's tail surfaces

events.text: Flight 498 began its descent into Los Angeles with 58 passengers and 6 crew members
The Piper collided nearly perpendicular to the upper left side of the horizontal stabilizer support structure of the DC-9
The collision sheared off the top of the Piper's cockpit and decapitated the pilot and both passengers
The DC-9, with its horizontal stabilizer, rudder, and half of its vertical stabilizer torn off, over-banked to the right and entered a steep dive

title: Pan Am 73
summary: Pan American World Airways Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground at Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, Pakistan, on September 5, 1986. Four armed Palestinian militants of the Abu Nidal Organization, dressed as Pakistani airport security personnel, rushed the aircraft with assault rifles, grenades, and explosives. The hijackers bypassed airport security by driving a van modified to look like an official security vehicle through a security checkpoint. The cockpit crew exited the aircraft through an overhead emergency hatch, immobilizing the aircraft. More than twenty passengers were killed during the hijacking, including nationals from India, the United Kingdom, Italy, Pakistan, and Mexico. All hijackers were arrested and initially sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment.
probable_cause: Security gaps at Karachi airport allowed hijackers dressed as security personnel to approach the aircraft. The aircraft was hijacked by four armed Palestinian militants who sought to use the hijacked airliner for political purposes, resulting in multiple passenger deaths and a hostage situation resolved by Pakistani authorities.

factors.evidence: The hijackers drove a van that had been modified to look like an airport security vehicle, fitted with a siren and flashing lights, and went through a security checkpoint up to one of the boarding stairways.
Four armed Palestinian militants of the Abu Nidal Organization hijacked the aircraft at Karachi while on the ground, armed with assault rifles, grenades, and plastic explosive belts.
The cockpit crew exited the aircraft through the overhead emergency hatch, immobilizing the aircraft and preventing the hijackers from flying it.
The aircraft remained on the ground throughout the hijacking; more than 360 passengers survived despite the hostage situation and violence.

events.text: Four hijackers dressed as Karachi airport security guards drove a van modified to look like a security vehicle through a security checkpoint to the aircraft.
Hijackers rushed the aircraft firing shots into the air and forcing a flight attendant to close the door; Senior Purser Neerja Bhanot relayed the hijack code to the cockpit.
The cockpit crew exited the aircraft through the overhead emergency hatch via the Inertial Reel Escape Device after receiving the hijack code.
After approximately 40 minutes, all four hijackers were arrested by Pakistani authorities; hijackers were initially sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment.

notes: Airport security gap enabled hijackers to approach aircraft
More than 360 passengers survived despite violence

title: 1986 Mozambican Tupolev Tu-134 crash
summary: A Tupolev Tu-134 with President Samora Machel and 43 others departed Mbala, Zambia at 18:38 for Maputo. The navigator used Doppler navigation to turn the aircraft based on a VOR signal, but inadvertently tuned the VOR receiver to Matsapa Airport in Swaziland instead of Maputo. This placed the aircraft on a navigation path 45° off course. The crew failed to monitor the correct VOR or cross-check their position and continued the descent. The captain did not respond to ground proximity warnings. The aircraft crashed at Mbuzini, South Africa.
probable_cause: Loss of control and impact with terrain due to erroneous navigation caused by crew tuning the VOR receiver to the wrong frequency, inadequate monitoring of navigation systems, and failure to respond to ground proximity warnings.

factors.evidence: Poor design of VOR frequency display with no back-lighting, unusually close frequencies, and similar appearance of displayed numerals made frequency selection error more likely
Crew set first VOR receiver to Matsapa frequency instead of Maputo frequency, diverting aircraft 45 degrees off course
Second VOR receiver correctly set to Maputo but apparently not being used or monitored by crew
Board concluded captain failed to react to ground proximity warning system
crashed at Mbuzini, South Africa

events.text: Departed Mbala for non-stop return to Maputo; weather forecast favorable, estimated time of arrival 21:25
Navigator performed 37-degree turn using autopilot Doppler navigation mode after observing VOR signal indicating interception of Maputo VOR 45-degree radial
Turn placed aircraft on path following 45-degree radial from Matsapa Airport VOR in Swaziland instead of Maputo
Captain re-tuned first VOR receiver to ILS frequency; second VOR correctly displaying Maputo position but not being monitored
Aircraft descended into terrain with ground proximity warning system activated; captain did not respond appropriately

notes: detailed technical analysis provided by board of inquiry

title: Aeroflot 6502
summary: Aeroflot Flight 6502 from Yekaterinburg to Grozny was on approach to Kurumoch Airport in Samara. The captain made a bet with the first officer that he could conduct an instrument-only approach with curtained cockpit windows instead of the NDB approach suggested by air traffic control. The captain ignored the ground-proximity warning at 62 meters altitude and did not execute the suggested go-around. The aircraft touched down at 150 knots and overran the runway, coming to rest upside down. Of 94 occupants, 68 died in the crash and 7 more died in hospitals.
probable_cause: The captain deliberately attempted an unauthorized instrument-only approach with cockpit windows curtained, ignoring ground-proximity warnings and air traffic control guidance to execute a go-around. This deliberate act of negligence and the crew's failure to respond appropriately to terrain warnings resulted in excessive speed landing and runway overrun.

factors.evidence: The captain made a bet with the first officer that he could make an instrument-only approach with curtained cockpit windows, deliberately deviating from the suggested NDB approach.
The captain ignored the ground-proximity warning at an altitude of 62 meters and did not make the suggested go-around.
The captain did not execute the go-around suggested by air traffic control despite the ground-proximity warning.
The aircraft touched down on the runway at a speed of 150 knots, which was excessive for landing and led to runway overrun.
The aircraft touched down on the runway at a speed of 150 knots and came to rest upside down after overrunning the runway.

events.text: The captain made a bet with the first officer that he could make an instrument-only approach with curtained cockpit windows instead of the NDB approach suggested by air traffic control.
Ground-proximity warning activated at an altitude of 62 meters.
The captain ignored the ground-proximity warning and did not execute the suggested go-around.
The aircraft touched down on the runway at a speed of 150 knots and came to rest upside down after overrunning the runway.

notes: Deliberate act (bet) was clearly primary cause
Captain prosecuted and sentenced to 15 years
Fatalities: 68 in crash, 7 more in hospitals

title: Aeroflot 892
summary: Aeroflot Flight 892 from Minsk to Berlin was diverted to Prague due to adverse weather. Upon return to Berlin, the crew misidentified the closed runway 25R as the landing runway due to a language barrier in understanding a controller's English warning about test lighting. Ground control warnings went unnoticed during cockpit discussion. When the error was realized, the crew changed course and engaged the autopilot but failed to increase thrust, causing an aerodynamic stall. The aircraft crashed into trees approximately 3 km from the runway threshold.
probable_cause: Crew misidentified the landing runway due to inadequate English language proficiency and inability to understand the controller's radio warning. The recovery procedure lacked necessary thrust application, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and controlled flight into terrain.

factors.evidence: Due to the radio operator's lack of English proficiency, the warning that test lights were on runway 25R was misunderstood to mean the aircraft was cleared to land on that runway.
The pilot manually changed course to runway 25R, which was 460 meters to the right of the cleared runway 25L.
The error was noticed on the ground but warnings went unnoticed for some time due to discussion among the crew.
The crew failed to recognize or respond to ground control warnings regarding their incorrect runway alignment.
Upon realizing the error, the crew changed course and engaged autopilot without increasing thrust, which was required for a safe recovery.
The Tu-134 stalled during the attempted recovery due to insufficient thrust.
The aircraft struck trees approximately 3 km from runway 25L's threshold.

events.text: Controller cleared the flight to land on runway 25L but the runway lights for runway 25R were turned on for testing.
Pilot disengaged autopilot and manually changed the course to runway 25R, which was 460 meters to the right of runway 25L.
Ground control warned the aircraft about the error but the warnings went unnoticed for some time due to discussion among the crew.
Once the crew realized their mistake, they rapidly changed course and engaged the autopilot but did not increase the thrust of the aircraft's engines.
The Tu-134 stalled and struck trees some 3 km from runway 25L's threshold.

notes: Language barrier confirmed as primary cause
